correctness.rationale: Poisson Leibniz identities force the bracket-derived line to annihilate the product. All compatible nonzero multiplications correspond to nonzero symmetric binary forms S; T=J^{-1}S is traceless. The full isomorphism relation is T similarity, with q^2 central shears. Simultaneous Poisson derivations correspond to A commuting with T plus two shears. Rational canonical form gives exactly q odd-field classes and 2q-1 even-field classes; centralizer classifications yield all orders and derivation dimensions. verify.py independently enumerates fields of sizes 2,3,4,5 and returns VERIFY_OK. The computations support but do not prove the all-field claim.

value.rationale: The problem is the complete class of nontrivial associative products whose square lies in the Heisenberg bracket-derived ideal on the minimal nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra, not an arbitrary coefficient slice. The theorem classifies all its finite-field symmetry strata and explains the precise characteristic-two jump: products proportional to the alternating bracket admit the full four-dimensional matrix symmetry, giving two additional Poisson derivations. The complete q and 2q-1 class counts and exact stabilizer sizes are natural finite-field invariants relevant to deformations, automorphisms and moduli.
